item.title: Asian Stocks to Gain on Lower Oil, US Bonds Rally: Markets Wrap
item.description: Asian stocks and bonds were set to track a rally on Wall Street as a pullback in oil prices eased inflation concerns. The yen was steady ahead of the Bank of Japan’s interest-rate decision.
item.dc:creator: Toby Alder

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Sept. 18
item.description: Oil dropped for a third day as supply concerns eased and traders looked to the next round of diplomacy that’ll shape the US-Iran war.
item.dc:creator: Kanoko Matsuyama

item.title: 01.AI's Kai-Fu Lee on Pacing Frontier AI Development
item.description: Kai-Fu Lee, CEO of 01.AI, says he suspects American AI companies may already have developed models that are "really great, but also really scary." He discusses this on "Bloomberg: The China Show" on the sidelines of the BNP Paribas Global Markets APAC Conference. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Macerich CEO: Consumers Are Spending, but Are Selective
item.description: Macerich's President and CEO, Jack Hsieh, joins the program shortly after presenting at the Bank of America real estate conference. The segment is framed around Macerich and the broader theme of "tracking the shopping mall resurgence." He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Schwab Is Neutral on Equities, Favorable on Commodities, Sonders Says
item.description: Liz Ann Sonders, Charles Schwab chief investment strategist, says there is no one asset allocation that makes sense for every investor. She says the firm is neutral on equities, less favorable on fixed income, and more favorable on commodities. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: BNY Chief Economist on Fed Rate Hike, BOJ Outlook
item.description: Vincent Reinhart, Chief Economist over at BNY Investments, discusses the Bank of Japan’s upcoming rate decision due Friday. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: DoubleLine’s Gundlach Warns of Fiscal Crisis in Next Recession
item.description: DoubleLine Capital chief executive Jeffrey Gundlach warned that the next US downturn could trigger a debt crisis that sends long-term Treasury yields sharply higher — defying decades of conventional wisdom that bonds will always serve as safe haven during times of economic strife.
item.dc:creator: Greg Ritchie and Michael MacKenzie

item.title: US to Sell F-35s to Saudi Arabia in $24.3 Billion Deal
item.description:
The State Department notified Congress that it plans to sell Saudi Arabia up to 48 F-35 warplanes in a first-time sale that could be worth as much as $24.3 billion. The sale of the Lockheed Martin Corp. fighter jet to Saudi Arabia has been in the works for a number of years. President Donald Trump signaled in November the US would sell F-35s to the Kingdom, offering Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman a prize he’s long cherished, ahead of a visit to the White House that month. Meantime, the Pentagon and Lockheed Martin Corp. are moving to speed up the production of a new classified air-to-air missile for US Air Force and Navy jets that’s seen as vital to deterring China.
For more, we speak with Wayne Sanders, Senior Defense Research Analyst for Bloomberg Intelligence. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Jeni’s Splendid Ice Creams Founder on New Fiber Company
item.description: Jeni Britton, founder of Jeni’s Splendid Ice Creams and now Founder and CEO of Floura, discussed her shift from ice cream to fiber-based snacks made from produce trim like apple cores, watermelon rinds, mango and pineapple rinds. Britton highlighted Starbucks as an important validation point for the young company, saying the placement gives Floura higher visibility and credibility as it expands beyond its direct-to-consumer roots. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Carry Trade Explained: Why the Japanese Yen Is Losing Its Appeal (JPY/USD)
item.description: For decades, the Japanese yen has been one of the world’s favored currencies for investors looking to borrow cheaply and put that money into assets offering higher returns.
item.dc:creator: Masaki Kondo

item.title: Saudi Pivots Oil Routes After Pipeline Attack
item.description: Saudi Arabia is ramping up prompt sales of crude from outside the Strait of Hormuz following the shutdown of the kingdom’s East-West pipeline, which halted cross-country flows to its Red Sea coast. The sale helped attribute to a fall in oil prices as physical markets cooled from recent peaks as traders bet some Middle East supply outages would be short-lived. Noam Raydan, William Sudhaus Senior Fellow at the Washington Institute, joins Bloomberg Businessweek to discuss why the Saudi pipeline is so crucial and what the attack on the pipeline could mean for the broader Saudi oil industry. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Japan’s Retail Bond Boom Offers New Avenue for Fiscal Funding
item.description: Japan’s rising yields are drawing record demand for retail government bonds, offering a potential new source of funding just as policymakers seek to contain borrowing costs and reduce market supply.
item.dc:creator: Masaki Kondo

item.title: Suspended Glencore Executive Told Radiant ‘Say Nothing on Email’
item.description: A senior Glencore Plc executive last year urged counterparts at Radiant World not to communicate by email, according to WhatsApp messages from the company’s head of iron ore seen by Bloomberg News.
item.dc:creator: Jack Farchy and Thomas Biesheuvel

item.title: Small Town America Confronts Data Centers, Rejects Some Plans
item.description: Bloomberg's Shruti Singh joins Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Real Yield." Blackstone-owned QTS proposed a massive data center in Clinton, Iowa, that would bring thousands of construction jobs and provide nearly $200 million in property taxes in its first 10 years. Many residents though want nothing to do with the data center and view it as a potential source of noise pollution, environmental degradation and rising utility costs - rejecting what some fear will do more harm than good, even if that means sacrificing economic growth. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Braskem Creditors Shun Debt Plan, Push Owners to Inject Cash
item.description: Braskem SA’s bondholders are balking at a restructuring proposal presented by the petrochemical giant, increasing pressure on Petrobras to commit fresh capital into the business, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Giovanna Bellotti Azevedo, Rachel Gamarski and Matheus Piovesana

item.title: Generac Surges 18% on $8 Billion Amazon Data Center Deal | Closing Bell
item.description: Comprehensive cross-platform coverage of the U.S. market close on Bloomberg Television, Bloomberg Radio, and YouTube with Romaine Bostick, Isabelle Lee, Lisa Mateo, and Alexis Christoforous. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Shareholders Revolt After Crypto Hoarders’ $50 Billion Crash
item.description: Investors are ramping up scrutiny of how much crypto hoarders pay their employees, as shareholders nurse losses totaling about $50 billion.
item.dc:creator: Olga Kharif, Ryan Weeks and Muyao Shen

item.title: Gold Surges Along With US Treasuries as Oil Price Slide Deepens
item.description: Gold rallied alongside Treasuries as a slump in oil prices helped ease concerns about inflation, following the Federal Reserve’s first interest-rate hike since 2023.
item.dc:creator: Jack Ryan and Yihui Xie

item.title: Stocks, Bonds Rise After Fed-Day Drop as Oil Falls: Markets Wrap
item.description: Stocks joined bonds higher as falling oil prices lent support to optimism that inflation can be kept under control a day after the Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time since 2023.
item.dc:creator: Rita Nazareth

item.title: Oil Drops as Traders See Supply Outages Proving Short-Lived
item.description: Oil fell as physical markets cooled from recent peaks as traders bet some Middle East supply outages would be short-lived.
item.dc:creator: Will Kubzansky, Kanoko Matsuyama and Charles Gorrivan
